newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary confirms it will abolish customs surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Hungary confirms it will abolish customs surcharge.

text.p: The government approval of Hungary's draft 1997 budget left the country's plans to abolish its customs surcharge unchanged, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy told a news conference on Thursday.
"The government confirmed its intention to continue the reduction of the customs surcharge," he said.
Hungary introduced an eight percent surcharge in March 1995, as a part of an austerity package, which aimed at reining in the country's soaring budget and current account deficits.
Hungary cut the surcharge by one percentage point in July and announced recently that a further one percentage point reduction will follow on October 1.
Medgyessy said the surcharge will be abolished in stages by mid-1997, as previously scheduled.
Three reductions of two points each are planned for January 1, April 1 and June 30, 1997.
